summary: Backend testing of the 10 security/bug fixes from the AssocManager audit. Wrote 22 pytest tests covering all 10 items: exports (CSV/PDF), HTML/CSV injection guards, error messages, crypto tokens, year range validation, phone duplicate, public rate limit, CORS domains, Helmet headers, and email validation on members/admin/platform. 20/22 PASS. 2 real bugs surfaced: (a) POST /api/platform/superadmins lacks email format validation (audit item #10 partial coverage) — accepts 'invalid-format-xxx' and returns 201; (b) Express default JSON parse error leaks a full Node stack trace in the response body (audit item #3 not fully applied). All other fixes verified working: Helmet CSP/X-Frame-Options/X-Content-Type-Options headers present, obsolete CORS domain not echoed, escapeCsv prevents formula injection (=,+,-,@) in members export, escapeHtml applied on PDF export, /api/public/deletion-request returns 429 after 5 requests, year 1999/2101/negative/zero all rejected 400, member and admin/create + platform association-admin endpoints all reject invalid emails with 'Format email invalide', duplicate phone rejected 400, crypto.randomBytes produces base64url tokens of len>=20.

minor.issue: Missing email format validation. Accepts 'invalid-format' as email and returns 201. All other 'create-*' endpoints already have the regex /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/. Please add the same check before creating the SuperAdmin (routes/platform.js around line 177). Audit fix #10 was applied to routes/members.js, routes/admin.js, routes/platform.js line 510 (association-admin creation) but NOT to routes/platform.js line 173 (superadmin creation).

minor.endpoint: Any POST/PUT with malformed JSON body (tested via /api/members)
minor.issue: Express default error handler serializes SyntaxError including its 'stack' field, exposing the full Node internal stack trace (paths to /app/backend/node_modules/body-parser/lib/types/json.js:169:10, etc.). Audit fix #3 (clean error messages) not fully applied. Add a global JSON-parse error middleware, e.g.: app.use((err, req, res, next) => { if (err.type === 'entity.parse.failed') return res.status(400).json({ error: 'JSON invalide' }); next(err); }); AND a final error handler that never returns err.stack.

action_items: Add email regex validation in routes/platform.js POST /superadmins handler (around line 177) mirroring the check already present at line 509. Return 400 { error: 'Format email invalide' }.

Add a global body-parser JSON error handler in server.js to catch entity.parse.failed and return a clean 400 without exposing the stack. Also ensure the final error handler strips 'stack' from responses in production.
critical_code_review_comments: Positive: helmet(), rate limiters (loginLimiter 5/15min and deletionLimiter 5/60min), escapeHtml/escapeCsv helpers, crypto.randomBytes(24).toString('base64url') for tokens are all implemented correctly and verified end-to-end.
Positive: Year validation is strict (Number.isInteger + 2000-2100 range + amount>0 + amount<100_000_000). Phone duplicate check on POST /api/members is present and effective.
Positive: Members export CSV correctly escapes cells whose first char is =, +, -, @, \t, \r by prepending a single quote — confirmed on live export.

Gap: Email validation is inconsistent across route files. Same regex is duplicated 4 times (members.js:89, admin.js:49, platform.js:509) but missing in platform.js:177 (superadmin creation). Consider extracting to /app/backend/utils/validators.js as a single `isValidEmail(email)` helper and reusing it.

Gap: Express server.js has no explicit error middleware. When body-parser fails on malformed JSON it defaults to Express's finalhandler which returns { error, stack } (line count matches Node 20). Add: app.use((err, req, res, next) => { if (err.type?.startsWith('entity.')) return res.status(400).json({ error: 'Requête invalide' }); ... }).

Consideration: CSP header is very restrictive (default-src 'self'). If the /api/exceptional/pdf or /api/export/stats/pdf HTML pages are loaded in an <iframe> or opened via window.open (parametres.js), the frame-ancestors 'self' and script-src 'self' may still block the inline print helpers. Worth a quick UI smoke check on the export flow — this is beyond backend scope though.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Test file: /app/backend/tests/test_security_fixes.py, 22 tests, 20 passing. To re-run: `cd /app/backend/tests && python -m pytest test_security_fixes.py -v --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/security_fixes.xml`. IMPORTANT: If tests report 429 on login, `sudo supervisorctl restart backend` to clear the in-memory loginLimiter (5 attempts / 15 min per IP). Backend URL: https://mobile-bug-crush-1.preview.emergentagent.com. The 2 remaining failures (test_platform_superadmin_invalid_email_format and test_invalid_json_body) will pass once the main agent adds (a) email regex in platform.js POST /superadmins, and (b) a JSON-parse error middleware in server.js.
rca_of_the_issue: Audit item #10 (email validation) — the developer duplicated the regex check in 3 of 4 create endpoints but forgot POST /api/platform/superadmins. RCA: no shared validator utility. Mitigation: extract regex to shared helper. Audit item #3 (clean error messages) — the developer likely handled per-route error responses (they all return { error: '...' }) but did not add a global Express error middleware, so body-parser SyntaxError falls through to Express's default finalhandler which JSON-serializes the Error including .stack. RCA: no centralized error handler in server.js. Mitigation: add app.use((err, req, res, next) => { ... }) at bottom of server.js.
